deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building the localization C[W^{-1}] of a category with weak equivalences and a class of 'cofibrations' (a structure close to Brown's categories of cofibrant objects or Waldhausen/Baues cofibration categories). He does it through categories of one-step 'paths' (chemins).

The construction:
- For objects x, y, the category Ch_0(x,y) has as objects the cospans x --f--> y' <--i-- y, where i is a trivial cofibration (marked ~). Its morphisms are maps y' -> y'' compatible with f and i.
- Composition Ch_0(y,z) x Ch_0(x,y) -> Ch_0(x,z) is defined by pushout (cocartesian square). The pushout of the trivial cofibration along f is again a trivial cofibration.
- This composition is associative only up to canonical isomorphism. It has strict two-sided identities 1_x = (x --1--> x <--1-- x), obtained by normalizing the choice of pushouts along identities.
- There are functors Hom_C(x,y)_discrete -> Ch_0(x,y), f |-> (f, id), compatible with composition.

Passing to components:
- Set pi_0(x,y) := pi_0(Ch_0(x,y)), the set of connected components of the category.
- Since pi_0 preserves products and identifies canonically isomorphic objects, the composition descends to a strictly associative composition ('ouf!!') with units the classes of 1_x.
- This gives a category C~ and a functor C -> C~ that is the identity on objects.

He remarks that nothing about (C,W) has been used yet. In a bracket he notes that the minimal hypothesis needed is a class 'cof' with cof ∩ W = trivial cofibrations; a full cofibration structure is not required.

The theorem he begins: C -> C~ sends every f in W to an isomorphism.
- Given f: x -> y in W, he seeks g: y -> x' and a trivial cofibration i: x -> x' such that the class of (gf, i) is the component of 1_x in pi_0(Ch_0(x,x)).
- He also needs the class of (f'g, j) to be the component of 1_y.
- Here j: y -> y' and f': x' -> y' come from the pushout of f along i.
- The page breaks off at this point, so the proof is unfinished here.

The evident aim is the universal property: C~ = C[W^{-1}], i.e. Ho(C)(x,y) = pi_0 of the category of cospans x -> y' <~ y. This is the cospan/fraction description of the homotopy category of a cofibration category.

The subscript 0 in Ch_0 suggests higher Ch_n, or the nerves of these categories, as models of mapping spaces. That would be in the spirit of Dwyer–Kan, but nothing of the sort is written on this page.
errors: The functor Hom_C(x,y) -> Ch_0(x,y) is written f |-> (f, id_x); for a cospan x -> y <- y the second component should be id_y (slip of notation).
Strict two-sided identities require a normalized choice of pushouts (pushout along an identity chosen to be the identity). This is implicit but harmless.
For pi_0 composition to be well defined one needs the pushout composition to be functorial in morphisms of Ch_0, which holds via the universal property. This is unstated but fine.

Proving that W maps to isomorphisms needs more hypotheses than stated (2-out-of-3, a factorization or Brown-type lemma, and some cofibrancy). The page stops before these are invoked, so the argument is incomplete here.

ideas.what: Hom-sets of the localization as pi_0 of a category of cospans x -> y' <~ y with trivial-cofibration backward leg, composed by pushout
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy category of a cofibration category / category of cofibrant objects via (co)fractions; one-step hammock localization
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gabriel–Zisman (1967, calculus of fractions); K. S. Brown (1973, categories of fibrant objects); Dwyer–Kan (1980, hammocks); Baues (1989, cofibration categories); Cisinski, Rădulescu-Banu (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Related localizer and modelizer discussions appear in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and Les Dérivateurs; this exact construction is not known to me in published form

ideas.what: Minimal axiom: a class cof with cof ∩ W equal to the trivial cofibrations, without full model structure
ideas.modern_name: Cofibration category / Waldhausen category with weak equivalences (weakened axioms)

ideas.what: Strictification: a composition associative only up to canonical isomorphism becomes strictly associative after pi_0
ideas.modern_name: Truncation of a bicategory-like structure to its homotopy category

missed.claim: A dated (printout paper from August 1982, so before Pursuing Stacks) record of Grothendieck independently developing the cospan/pushout description of Ho(C) for a cofibration-type structure with weakened axioms. Indexing by Ch_0 hints that he intended higher Ch_n (mapping spaces), but that is not developed here.
missed.quote: Pour l'instant, on n'a utilisé rien sur (C, W) ... un cof pas même = cof w, tel que cof ∩ W = cofibr. W
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical only: it documents Grothendieck's pre-Pursuing-Stacks work on abstract homotopy theory. The mathematics is standard (Brown, Dwyer–Kan, Baues).

deep.surprise_reason: A standard construction of the homotopy category via cospans and pushouts, known from Brown and Dwyer–Kan and later Baues. It is of modest historical interest as an early-1982 Grothendieck sketch with minimal axioms, but there is no new mathematics on the page.
transcription_corrections: '(f, id_x)' as written by Grothendieck is presumably intended as (f, id_y).

'dans les composants' is more likely 'dans les composantes' (connected components); the sentence reads roughly 'passant aux composantes, la composition des Ch_0 définit une composition des pi_0(x,y)'.
The category is written C~ (with an asterisk/footnote mark), and the functor is C -> C~.
In the final diagram the pushout square is x --f~--> y, i: x ~> x', j: y ~> y', f': x' --~--> y', labelled '(cocart.)'.
